profiles.title: Permission profiles
profiles.intro: A profile defines which panel modules an account can access and at what level (a higher level includes the lower ones). An account has one profile (chosen in Users). A profile with the change right in the “Users and security” module is a panel administrator – the panel will not let you end up without an active one.
profiles.idTaken: a profile with this identifier already exists
profiles.name: Name
profiles.adminWarning: The change right in “Users and security” makes the profile a panel administrator: creating accounts, assigning profiles (also to oneself), the MFA requirement.
profiles.deleteText: A profile without assigned accounts. The change is recorded in the audit log.

builtinDesc.admin: full access, including accounts, profiles and security settings

builtinDesc.viewer: read-only access to alerts, events, rules and system health

ldap.title: Domain sign-in
ldap.intro: Active Directory accounts sign in to the panel with their own username and password (LDAPS – encrypted). Access and the permission profile come from AD groups: the first matching mapping on the list decides. Membership is checked at sign-in and every 5 minutes – removal from the group or disabling the account in AD ends the sessions. The second factor (TOTP) applies as for local accounts; the local administrator account stays as a break-glass account.
ldap.urlsHint: ldaps://dc01.contoso.com:636 – one per line (the next ones are fallbacks)
ldap.serverNameHint: when the address is an IP or a name not in the controller certificate
ldap.caHint: e.g. an export of the AD CS authority certificate; empty – the system's trusted certificates
ldap.bindHint: read-only, e.g. svc-vardr@contoso.com or its DN
ldap.baseHint: where to look for accounts, e.g. DC=contoso,DC=com
ldap.testOk: the LDAPS connection and the service account sign-in work
ldap.groupsIntro: Create groups for the panel in your own OU in AD (any names), enter the OU and choose a profile for the groups. Groups are identified by SID – renaming them in AD breaks nothing. Nested membership counts too.
ldap.mappings: Mappings (order decides – the first match wins):
ldap.noMappings: None – no domain account can sign in to the panel.
ldap.notFound: No such account in the account base.
ldap.willGet: At sign-in they get the profile “{{profile}}” (group {{group}}).
ldap.noLogin: Cannot sign in – not a member of any mapped group.
ldap.saveText: The change is recorded in the audit log (without passwords) and takes effect immediately.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.intro: A token lets a program (a script, an integration, an MCP server) use the panel API with the Authorization: Bearer header. A token has a permission profile like an account, but it cannot manage accounts, profiles or tokens, and operations that require a password are not available to it. Every change made with a token is recorded in the audit log as api:<name>.
tokens.disabled: API tokens are not available in this server configuration.
tokens.nameHint: 2–64 characters: letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore – shown in the audit log as api:<name>
tokens.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. exporting alerts to the ticketing system
tokens.profileHint: Grant only what the integration needs – usually read access.
tokens.adminWarning: The administrator profile gives the token full access to data and settings (without account management). A stolen token is a stolen panel – consider a narrower profile.
tokens.secretText: Copy the token and store it in the program's configuration (e.g. in a secrets manager).
tokens.secretOnce: The panel shows it only now – the database keeps only its hash.
tokens.revokeText: The program using this token loses access immediately. This cannot be undone – create a new token if needed. The change is recorded in the audit log.
tokens.historyIntro: Every request made with this token: method, path with parameters, result and response time. The history is kept for {{days}} days; permission denials are also in the audit log.

notify.added: Channel added – send a test to check the address.
notify.title: Notifications
notify.intro: Channels to which Vardr sends messages outside the system: detection alerts, incidents, health alerts (from Grafana) and the daily Urd archive anchor{{at}} – the hash of the latest manifest, whose copy at the recipient is independent proof of the archive's integrity. The webhook address is a secret: the panel shows only its beginning and end. Message language – below (“System language”).
notify.noRelay: Grafana alerts are not relayed – siem-api has no SIEM_ALERT_RELAY_TOKEN.
notify.noAlertChannel: No enabled channel receives detection alerts (Gjallarhorn) – alerts are only in the panel. Tick “{{event}}” on the channel that should receive them.
notify.noChannels: No channels yet – alerts and the anchor go nowhere. Add e.g. a Discord channel webhook (Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy URL).
notify.narrowing: narrowing the alerts sent to the channel
notify.name: Name
notify.urlDiscord: https://discord.com/api/webhooks/… – treat it like a password
notify.urlWebhook: https://… – Vardr sends a POST with JSON {event, severity, title, text, fields, at}
notify.confirmText: {{what}} – this change limits what leaves the system (e.g. archive anchors), so it requires your password.
notify.systemLanguageHelp: Language of notifications (alerts, incidents, Grafana health alerts, archive anchor) and the default language of NIS2 report drafts. Each account sees the panel in its own language. The change is recorded in the audit log.
notify.urlTeams: The HTTP trigger address of a Power Automate flow (e.g. the Teams template “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”) – https://….logic.azure.com/workflows/… or https://….api.powerplatform.com/…; treat it like a password
notify.signHelp: X-Vardr-Timestamp and X-Vardr-Signature headers – the recipient can check that Vardr sent the message. The panel shows the secret once, after saving.
notify.unsignLabel: disabling message signing (a recipient that checks the signature will reject further messages)
notify.newSecretLabel: a new signing secret (the current one stops working at the recipient)
notify.secretText: Copy the secret and set it at the recipient (in the flow, function or service that checks the signature).
notify.secretOnce: The panel shows it only now.
notify.secretHow: Signature: HMAC-SHA256 with the secret over “<X-Vardr-Timestamp>.<body>”, header X-Vardr-Signature: sha256=<hex>. Reject messages with a timestamp older than a few minutes. Details and an example: the panel documentation (Notifications).
